title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes a snapshot of 749 customers, revealing an overall churn rate of 37.7%. The analysis identifies contract type and customer support experience as critical drivers of churn. Monthly contracts exhibit significantly higher churn than annual contracts. A specific at-risk segment with high support tickets and low satisfaction shows a churn rate nearly double the average. Lifetime value scales substantially with plan tier, highlighting the revenue impact of retention strategies.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers. The overall churn rate is 37.7%, and the average monthly fee is $42.11.
Churn rates are relatively stable across plan types, ranging from 36.6% for Premium to 38.9% for Basic. Basic plan customers experience the highest churn.
Churn rates by signup cohort show slight variation, with the 2024 cohort having the highest churn rate at 39.8% and the 2022 cohort the lowest at 36.7%.
Monthly contracts have a churn rate of 48.3%, which is 121.1% higher than the 21.9% rate for Annual contracts.
An at-risk segment of 100 customers with high support tickets and low satisfaction exhibits a churn rate of 71.0%, which is 33.4 percentage points higher than the overall average.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months with a median of 19 months. The average satisfaction score is 3.42, though 27 records are missing this value.
Lifetime value (LTV) increases significantly by plan, with Premium LTV ($1,817) being 292.0% higher than Basic LTV ($463).

limitations: The analysis is based on a single snapshot and does not track customer behavior over time.
Satisfaction scores are missing for 27 customers, which may bias the satisfaction mean.
The dataset does not include demographic details, limiting segmentation possibilities.
conclusion: To reduce churn, the business should prioritize converting monthly customers to annual contracts and address the at-risk segment with targeted support interventions. The high LTV of Premium customers justifies investment in retention strategies for this tier.
